verses.commentary: A basket of ripe fruit. The fourth vision. Hebrew wordplay: qayits (summer fruit) sounds like qets (end). Visual pun announcing conclusion.
What do you see? A basket of ripe fruit. The time is ripe for my people Israel. Ready for harvest means ready for judgment. No more sparing. The end has come.
Temple songs become wailing. Many bodies flung everywhere. Then silence. The noise of death followed by the silence of death. Worship space becomes morgue.
You who trample the needy. The charge resumes. Doing away with the poor of the land. Systematic elimination of the vulnerable. Commerce as warfare against the weak.

When will the New Moon be over? When will the Sabbath end? They observe holy days impatiently, eager to return to cheating. Skimping measures, boosting prices, dishonest scales. Religious observance as interruption to fraud.
Buying the poor for silver, the needy for sandals. Debt slavery for trivial amounts. Selling sweepings with the wheat. Mixing chaff with grain. Every transaction an exploitation.
The Lord swears by the Pride of Jacob. Usually a divine title, here perhaps ironic: by the very pride that condemns them. I will never forget. Their deeds are permanently recorded.
Will not the land tremble? The earthquake anticipated in 1:1 now explained. The whole land rises and falls like the Nile's flood. Cosmic upheaval for covenantal violation.
The sun goes down at noon. Eclipse imagery. Darkness at brightest hour. Nature itself mourns Israel's judgment. What should be light becomes dark.
Festivals become mourning, songs become weeping. Celebration reversed. Sackcloth and shaved heads: full mourning rites. Like mourning an only son. The deepest grief imaginable. A bitter end.
A famine of hearing the words of the Lord. Not bread famine, not water thirst. Worse: silence from heaven. They silenced the prophets; God silences himself. The worst judgment is God's withdrawal.

They will stagger from sea to sea, wander from north to east. Frantic search for God's word. But they will not find it. The word they rejected becomes the word they cannot find. Too late to seek what they spurned.
Lovely young women and strong young men faint from thirst. The best of the nation collapsing. Not physical thirst but spiritual dehydration. Youth and beauty cannot survive without God's word.

Those who swear by the sin of Samaria. The golden calf at Bethel, called the sin. Oaths by the god of Dan and Beersheba. The idols they trusted cannot save. They will fall, never to rise again. Final collapse for those who chose false gods.
